thread:
infra-bot: ALERT: surge detected on hosted gateway /v1/generate -> multiple customer 504s and 5xx. Request queue depth p95 = 2200, continuous-batcher backlog rising. region=us-west1, model=redwood-medium-1. See logs: https://internal.logs/redwood/7448765432 :rotating_light:
Samir: seeing the same on console. gateway cpu ~92%, batcher threads blocked waiting on kvcache reads, dequeue rate falling behind. lots of small short requests from a few tenants.
Alex J: any recent deploys or config changes in us-west?
Maria L: no deploys in the last 6h. quota autoscale didn't trigger new workers, looks like we hit thin-pool cap (burst_limit). Checking autoscaler events now.
Theo: pinging the tenant list — looks like one customer (acme-retail) sending fanout short requests in a loop. Could be retry storm.
Ops Alice: flagged support ticket from Acme. They report 504s starting ~12:03 PDT. They've got parallelism=50 on client side.
Samir: throwing quick probes:
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -d '{"prompt":"hi","max_tokens":8}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
> 504 gateway timeout
```
Samir: stack shows queue wait times in request_router: avg_wait=120ms, p99_wait=2.1s, but dequeue spikes to 8-12s for tail requests.
Alex J: hypothesis: continuous-batcher is trying to pack small requests into large batches, causing KV cache pressure and long tail queues. If many tiny requests flood, the batcher waits to fill batches and pends requests.
Maria L: runbook suggests immediate mitigations: 1) enable per-tenant rate limit enforcement 2) reduce batcher max_wait_ms for the model 3) route heavy tenants to a low-latency fallback variant.
Theo: can we throttle acme-retail at gateway for now? Ops Alice, can you ask support to apply tenant throttle?
Ops Alice: I've applied a soft throttle (parallelism=10) for acme-retail and notified them. Watching metrics.
Samir: after throttle: queue depth p95 dropped from 2200 -> 900 in 60s, 5xx count dropping. tail dequeue times down to 2-3s.
Alex J: good. As a medium-term fix we should lower continuous-batcher window for redwood-medium-1 in us-west1 and disable wait-for-fill for small payload sizes. Maria, can you push that config with safe defaults?
Maria L: making change now: setting batcher.max_wait_ms: 40 -> 15 for model:redwood-medium-1 in us-west1. Also adding payload_size cutoff 512 bytes to bypass batcher. Patching via infra config path.
Maria L: applied. Canary rollout to 10% of hosts.
Samir: can confirm canary hosts show much lower per-request latency, dequeue backlog gone on those hosts.
Theo: any reason we shouldn't flip to 100%?
Alex J: wait for 10m to validate no regression on throughput/cost. Also schedule automatic fallback for quantized variant in case of resource thrash.
Ops Alice: customers reporting improved success rates. Support closing urgent ticket but leaving monitoring alerts.
Maria L: follow-ups: create alert for batcher.wait_growth rate, add tenant hot-spot detector (high small-request-parallelism), and add a KB article for support on applying tenant throttles.
Samir: logging note: captured request traces and KV-cache hit/miss distribution during the spike. Will attach to incident doc.
Alex J: thanks team. Opening incident postmortem and action items: (1) tenant hot-spot detection work (2) default batcher tuning for small-payload patterns (3) better autoscale headroom for thin-pool bursts (4) runbook update for tenant throttling steps.
infra-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated -> partial-resolved. Alert suppressed for 30m while we validate. runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/queue-surge.
Ops Alice: marking this thread resolved for now. Reopen if p95 queue depth > 1500 again. :white_check_mark:
